title: SDK resilient defaults: transport-aware backoffs, idempotency semantics, and stream-resume recipes
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Problem: SDK users need predictable, low-latency behavior from Python/TypeScript/Go clients when transient failures happen. Current cross-SDK guidance is fragmented: different backoff defaults, inconsistent idempotency key usage, and unclear streaming resume semantics lead to duplicate requests, wasted tokens, and poor developer experience.

Goal: Define and implement a pragmatic cross-language policy that is transport-aware (different defaults for HTTP vs gRPC), preserves safety for non-idempotent endpoints, and provides simple streaming resume primitives with guarded resume tokens. Produce examples for Python/TS/Go and land cross-SDK helpers that are easy to adopt in apps and frameworks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Documented transport-aware default profiles (http, websocket/grpc, unreliable mobile networks) with example parameter values.
2) Idempotency key policy: header name, key format, TTL, server-side behavior contract documented and implemented in each SDK.
3) SDK helper library shipped: generate_idempotency_key(), default_retry_profile(), stream_resumer() or equivalent in Python/TS/Go.
4) Tests and integration examples for a typical generation endpoint and a resumable streaming embeddings endpoint.
5) Backwards-compatible opt-out flags for projects that want existing behavior.
6) PRs merged and release notes drafted for sdks-2026.03.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
- Profile model: three named profiles: conservative (suitable for non-idempotent ops by default), balanced (default for most users), aggressive (used for idempotent bulk ops). Each profile is a set: initial_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, multiplier, jitter_pct, max_attempts, retryable_error_categories.
- Transport awareness: HTTP clients should treat 429 and 503 as retryable with the balanced profile; TCP-level connection resets and ECONNRESET are retryable at the client socket layer. gRPC streams should map UNAVAILABLE -> retryable, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED -> rate-limit handling with backoff, CANCELLED needs contextual decisioning (do not retry by default).
- Idempotency key rules: header: "Idempotency-Key". Key format: uuid-v4 or base64 32 bytes; servers keep 72h TTL by default. For streaming or chunked uploads we recommend per-operation key + optional part-index suffix if clients want fine-grained de-dup semantics. SDK helper will expose a short API: generate_idempotency_key(prefix=None) and attach_idempotency_key(request, key).
- Stream resume: server will emit a stable resume token at periodic boundaries (e.g., every N tokens or on graceful checkpoint). SDKs will store the last-seen resume token, and on an immediate reconnect will call /resume with token and idempotency key. Resume token lifetime and semantics documented.
- Safety: Conservative defaults avoid automatic retries for requests that include non-idempotent instructions (file-writes or side effects). SDKs will detect common patterns: presence of explicit "operation=mutate" header, or a per-endpoint manifest (server-provided metadata) that marks endpoints as non-retriable.

Cross-language ergonomics:
- Python: small helpers in redwood.sdk.resilience (generate_idempotency_key, RetrySession) that wrap requests.Session or httpx.
- TypeScript: exports in @redwood/sdk/resilience with types and a middleware for fetch/fetch-like clients.
- Go: package resilience with BackoffPolicy struct and convenience DoWithRetry(ctx, client, req, opts).

Example snippets (illustrative):
Python:
from redwood.sdk.resilience import RetrySession, generate_idempotency_key
s = RetrySession(profile='balanced')
key = generate_idempotency_key('create')
resp = s.post(url, json=payload, headers={'Idempotency-Key': key})

TypeScript:
import { defaultRetryProfile, generateIdempotencyKey } from '@redwood/sdk/resilience';
const client = new ResilientFetch({ profile: defaultRetryProfile });
const key = generateIdempotencyKey('create');
await client.post(url, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': key }, body: JSON.stringify(payload) });

Go:
policy := resilience.DefaultPolicy("balanced")
key := resilience.GenerateIdempotencyKey("create")
res, err := resilience.DoWithRetry(ctx, httpClient, req.WithContext(ctx), policy, map[string]string{"Idempotency-Key": key})

Edge cases & trade-offs:
- We do not attempt to infer idempotency from payload contents; that is error-prone. Instead, we provide opt-in flags and endpoint metadata.
- Automatic retries on CANCELLED or user-initiated disconnects are dangerous; default is conservative. Teams can opt-in for aggressive resume in batch workflows.
- For streaming, preserving exactly-once semantics is impossible without application-level support; we recommend at-least-once with idempotency markers and server-side dedup/merge behavior.

Telemetry: record retry profile, attempts, last_error_category, idempotency_key_present in SDK telemetry (opt-in).

2026-03-06 - Priya Shah (backend): Server will add endpoint metadata header X-Redwood-Retryable: true|false. Backend PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/server/pull/1456. Note: backend will store idempotency outcome for 72h by default, can be configured per-tenant.
2026-03-08 - Design review (Luca): Suggested we include example patterns for mobile intermittent networks and add a small doc section on battery/power-sensitive backoffs. Added as follow-up task.

2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: TS and Go prototypes ready for initial review. Tests flaky on graceful stream resume when server truncates token; adding guard and stricter validation. Planning to open cross-language RFC next week.
Review notes: Please check the conservative defaults for non-idempotent endpoints; PM wants minimal surprise for existing customers. Consider feature flag to enable aggressive resume per-tenant.
Security note: idempotency keys are sensitive in that they can reveal operation IDs; avoid logging them verbatim in high retention telemetry. Use hash-based telemetry or scrub.
